comparison: Both evaluate A. thaliana demographic inference (C82-C86, C108). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to documented model violations and cautions about reliability. Peer review also rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing sensitivity to whether epimutation rates are known vs. estimated and noting discrepancies with published rates.

Both address future potential and technological developments (C126-C129, C131-C133). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are aspirational goals rather than established results. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, endorsing the future potential given increasing data availability and new sequencing technologies.

Both evaluate simulation evidence for bottleneck recovery (C41-C46). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with detailed evidence from Figure 2 and Table 2. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, raising major caveat about strong dependence on knowing epimutation rates and questioning practical performance when rates must be estimated.

Both assess epimutation rate estimation accuracy (C52-C54). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting accuracy across different rates with documented limitations at high rates. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, highlighting that estimated rates differ substantially from published experimental values in real data.

Both evaluate demographic inference improvements with methylation data (C59-C62, C66). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with quantitative RMSE evidence. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting conditional performance depends on whether epimutation rates are known vs. estimated.

Both address site- and region-level epimutation processes (C71-C75, C95-C96). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with statistical tests and HMM evidence. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the analysis of empirical data and region-level methylation treatment.

Both evaluate core methodological framework (C4-C5, C88). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with simulation evidence. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, with reviewers explicitly endorsing the extension of SMC approaches and solid validation via simulation.

Both assess SMPs vs DMRs characteristics (C7, C79-C80 overlap). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, demonstrating rapid LD decay for SMPs and alignment with recombination patterns. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, accepting validation via simulation and empirical data, and acknowledging differential treatment of individual CGs vs regions.

Both evaluate DMR size issues (C8, C77-C78). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with quantitative evidence showing DMRs span multiple genealogies. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the distinction between individual CGs and regions in the empirical validation.

Both address model violations in A. thaliana data (C97-C99). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with LD pattern discrepancies and non-independence evidence. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the analysis of empirical data and implicitly acknowledging region-level processes.

Both evaluate practical recommendations (C115-C117). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with evidence from simulations. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, with reviewers noting caution about generalization beyond Arabidopsis and accepting current scope limitations.

Both address model limitations and future directions (C102-C104). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative research directions. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, acknowledging incomplete understanding and accepting that the method may hold more promise with better data.

Both evaluate cautionary statements about evolutionary forces (C109-C111). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED as well-justified caution based on documented violations. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, accepting this as foundation for further developments and acknowledging current limitations.

Both address differential performance based on known vs. estimated rates (C64-C65). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with clear evidence from supplementary figures. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting conditional performance creates uncertainty about practical utility.

Both evaluate mutation rate estimation (C90 overlap, C6 in OpenEval). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, showing accurate estimation across wide range with noted degradation at very high rates. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, highlighting discrepancies between estimated and published experimental rates.

Both address limitations and incomplete understanding (C100-C101). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED as appropriate cautionary statement. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, acknowledging incomplete knowledge of epigenetic mutational processes.
Minimal overlap (C6). OpenEval evaluates marker 2 mutation rate estimation as SUPPORTED. Peer review evaluates broader methodological framework as SUPPORTED, endorsing the SMC extension.

Minimal overlap (C63). OpenEval evaluates TMRCA inference improvement as SUPPORTED but modest. Peer review evaluates broader demographic inference as UNCERTAIN due to dependence on rate specification.

Minimal overlap (C67). OpenEval evaluates mislabeling effects as SUPPORTED with mechanistic explanation. Peer review evaluates broader demographic inference as UNCERTAIN due to conditional performance.

Both address biological interpretation (C113-C114). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation based on absence of conflicting signals weakened by model violations. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting current limitations as foundation for further work.

Minimal overlap (C81). OpenEval evaluates LD pattern discrepancies as SUPPORTED evidence for model violations. Peer review evaluates broader SMP/DMR characteristics as SUPPORTED through empirical validation.

OpenEval evaluates finite site modeling and LD utility for detecting violations (C91-C92) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological design features.

Peer review evaluates biological basis for using methylation as markers (C3, C28, C31-C35) as SUPPORTED, calling it intriguing addition for recent population history. No corresponding OpenEval result addresses these foundational biological premises.

Peer review evaluates motivation regarding SNP limitations for recent history (C2, C20, C22-C23) as SUPPORTED by all reviewers. No corresponding OpenEval result directly addresses this motivational premise.
